name: Aphthous ulcer
summary: A painful canker sore on the soft tissues inside the mouth. It is usually not contagious and often settles within 1–2 weeks.
care: Arrange an assessment if it lasts more than 2–3 weeks, keeps returning, is unusually large, or makes eating and drinking difficult.

name: Bleeding gums
summary: Bleeding, red, swollen or tender gums can be a sign of plaque-related gum irritation or another mouth problem.
care: Book a dental check if bleeding persists or comes with swelling, pain, bad breath or loose teeth.

name: Cheilitis
summary: Inflammation or irritation of the lips. Lips may look dry, cracked, red or scaly; the corners may also be affected.
care: Seek advice if it keeps returning, becomes hot or swollen, or does not improve. Rapid swelling or breathing difficulty is urgent.

name: Dental abscess
summary: A pocket of pus from infection in or around a tooth or gum. It may cause severe pain, swelling, fever, bad taste or pain with chewing.
care: Contact a dentist promptly. Facial or neck swelling, or trouble breathing, speaking or swallowing needs emergency help.

name: Enamel erosion
summary: Loss of the hard outer surface of a tooth, often related to acids from foods, drinks or reflux. Sensitivity and changes in tooth shape or colour can occur.
care: Arrange a dental assessment for persistent sensitivity, thinning or transparent-looking edges.

name: Fluorosis
summary: A change in the appearance of developing teeth caused by higher fluoride exposure while teeth are forming. It is not the same as tooth decay.
care: Ask a dentist to assess unusual white or brown markings rather than trying to treat them at home.

name: Gingivitis
summary: An early stage of gum disease that may cause red, swollen, tender or easily bleeding gums and persistent bad breath.
care: Arrange a dental appointment when gum bleeding or swelling continues so it can be assessed early.

name: Hypersensitivity
summary: A short, sharp response to hot, cold, sweet or acidic foods and drinks. It can have several dental causes.
care: Book a check if sensitivity is new, worsening, localised to one tooth or accompanied by pain.

name: Impacted wisdom tooth
summary: A wisdom tooth that does not have enough room to erupt normally. It may cause gum tenderness, food trapping, swelling or repeated infection.
care: Seek a dental assessment for recurring pain, swelling, bad taste or difficulty opening the mouth.

name: Jaw pain and TMJ symptoms
summary: Pain, stiffness, clicking or limited movement around the jaw joint can affect chewing and comfort. Several causes are possible.
care: Arrange an assessment for persistent pain, locking, injury or difficulty opening or closing the mouth.

name: Kids’ tooth decay
summary: Tooth decay can affect baby teeth as well as adult teeth. Early decay may be symptom-free before pain or visible changes appear.
care: Book regular child dental checks and seek advice for toothache, spots, sensitivity, swelling or feeding difficulty.

name: Leukoplakia
summary: A persistent white or grey patch in the mouth. It can have several causes and should not be self-diagnosed from a photograph.
care: Arrange a dental or medical assessment for any patch that does not clear, changes, hurts or bleeds.

name: Mouth ulcers
summary: Small sores can occur on the lips, cheeks, tongue, gums or palate. Many are short-lived, but recurring or persistent sores need review.
care: Seek advice if a sore lasts longer than 2–3 weeks, keeps returning, becomes very painful or affects eating.

name: Nerve-related tooth pain
summary: Deep or lingering tooth pain can occur when the inner pulp of a tooth is irritated. Similar symptoms can have different causes.
care: Arrange prompt dental assessment for spontaneous pain, lingering hot/cold pain or pain that interrupts sleep.

name: Oral thrush
summary: A Candida yeast overgrowth that may appear as white patches on a red mouth or tongue, with soreness or altered taste.
care: Contact a dentist or doctor for swallowing difficulty, a weakened immune system or symptoms that do not improve.

name: Periodontitis
summary: An advanced gum infection affecting the tissues and bone supporting teeth. Bleeding, receding gums, pus, bad breath or loose teeth may occur.
care: Arrange prompt dental review for persistent gum swelling, pus, receding gums, painful chewing or loose teeth.

name: Questions about oral health
summary: Bring a short list of symptoms, medicines, allergies and questions to your dental visit. Clear information helps the clinician plan the next step.
care: Use the booking form or ask the Gemini assistant for clinic hours, location and care pathways.

name: Root canal concerns
summary: Root canal treatment may be considered when the pulp inside a tooth is inflamed or infected. An examination is needed to understand the cause of pain.
care: Arrange a prompt assessment for severe toothache, lingering sensitivity, swelling or pain on biting.

name: Dry mouth
summary: Not enough saliva can cause a sticky feeling, soreness, swallowing difficulty and higher risk of tooth decay. Medicines and health conditions can contribute.
care: See a dentist or doctor if it lasts weeks, affects eating or comes with white patches, pain, dry eyes or frequent urination.

name: Tooth decay
summary: Plaque bacteria use sugars to create acids that gradually damage enamel. Early decay may have no symptoms; later signs include pain, sensitivity or a visible hole.
care: Arrange a dental check for toothache, sensitivity, spots or a hole, even if symptoms are mild.

name: Unhealed mouth sore
summary: A sore that does not heal is a reason to arrange an assessment. Persistent mouth changes can have many causes and are not automatically cancer.
care: Contact a dentist or doctor if a sore lasts 2–3 weeks, or sooner for a lump, red/white patch, numbness or swallowing difficulty.

name: Viral cold sores
summary: Cold sores are usually blisters on or around the lips and are different from canker sores inside the mouth. They can be contagious.
care: Ask a healthcare professional for advice if sores are frequent, severe, near the eye or accompanied by significant illness.

name: Wisdom teeth
summary: Wisdom teeth may be healthy and monitored, or may cause crowding, pain, infection or food trapping when they erupt without enough space.
care: Arrange an assessment for repeated pain, swelling, bad taste or difficulty opening the mouth.

name: X-rays in dental assessment
summary: Dental X-rays can help a clinician see areas that are not visible during a routine mouth examination. They are recommended only when clinically appropriate.
care: Ask the dentist why an image is recommended and what question it will help answer.

name: Yeast infection in the mouth
summary: Oral yeast overgrowth is commonly discussed as oral thrush. White patches, soreness or altered taste can have other causes too.
care: Arrange a dental or medical assessment instead of trying to diagnose a white patch from images alone.

name: Zero-delay urgent care
summary: Severe swelling, uncontrolled bleeding, breathing or swallowing difficulty, facial injury or a knocked-out tooth needs urgent professional guidance.
care: Call the clinic promptly at +91 9481731482; use emergency services for breathing difficulty or rapidly worsening swelling.
